endorsements.quote: To ensure quality, synthetic data should be compared with the original data to ensure proper labelling and inclusion of clinically significant cases and assessed for population diversity, intersectional fidelity, and intersectional hallucinations.

Finally, for model deployment, we highlight the need to quantify reidentification risks via k-anonymity tests 59 (k≥5) and membership inference advantage testing for privacy protection, continuous accuracy benchmarking against real-world baselines, and automated rejection of predictions relying predominantly (>50%) on synthetic features or high-risk variables.

unlisted_practices: Continuously incorporate real data during training when synthetic data are used to prevent model collapse.
Mandate disclosure of synthetic data algorithms, parameters, and source code to enable validation of clinical applicability.
Clearly label synthetic data as distinct from real data and restrict its use to exploratory analyses.
Do not use synthetic data as a standalone solution for data augmentation; supplement small-sample synthetic data with external datasets and transfer learning.
Have domain experts validate synthetic datasets to ensure they reflect population diversity.
Implement oversight mechanisms that prevent repeated synthetic data recursion without fresh real-world data and enforce transparency in synthetic data lineage.
Validate synthetic data against distributional metrics and clinician-led red-teaming for clinical plausibility before use.
Include performance deterioration indices, attribution layers weighting predictions by synthetic input source, and diversity preservation mechanisms during model development.
Adopt data hygiene practices such as outlier removal, temporal alignment, missing-data handling, and variable standardization for AI training data.
Adopt FAIR principles for data management.
Assess synthetic trust against predefined criteria for statistical fidelity, generalisability to underrepresented subgroups, and absence of privacy violations.
Evaluate synthetic data against alternatives such as federated learning or secure data enclaves before use.
Assess both inherited disparities from source data and new artifacts introduced during generation before clinical deployment of models using synthetic data.

screen.reason: This is a Viewpoint discussing the risks of synthetic data in healthcare AI and proposing actionable safeguards, standards, and deployment disclosures.
